questions.question: The clavicle is classified as a:

explanations.a: The clavicle is not classified as a flat bone.
explanations.b: The clavicle is not classified as a short bone.
explanations.c: The clavicle is classified as a long bone, although it has several unique features compared with other long bones.
explanations.d: The clavicle is not classified as an irregular bone.

questions.question: Which of the following makes the clavicle unique among long bones?

answers.b: It ossifies by endochondral ossification only
answers.d: It has an epiphysis at both ends

explanations.a: The clavicle does not have a typical medullary cavity like most long bones.
explanations.b: The clavicle undergoes both intramembranous and endochondral ossification.
explanations.c: The clavicle is unique among long bones because it lies horizontally and acts as a strut between the sternum and scapula.
explanations.d: The clavicle does not have typical epiphyses at both ends.

questions.question: The medial (sternal) end of the clavicle articulates with the:

explanations.a: The medial end of the clavicle does not directly articulate with the body of the sternum.
explanations.b: The medial or sternal end of the clavicle articulates with the manubrium of the sternum at the sternoclavicular joint.
explanations.c: The acromion articulates with the lateral end of the clavicle.
explanations.d: The coracoid process does not directly articulate with the clavicle.

questions.question: The lateral (acromial) end of the clavicle articulates with the:

explanations.a: The glenoid cavity articulates with the head of the humerus.
explanations.b: The coracoid process is related to the clavicle but does not form the acromioclavicular joint.
explanations.c: The lateral or acromial end of the clavicle articulates with the acromion of the scapula at the acromioclavicular joint.
explanations.d: The spine of the scapula does not directly articulate with the clavicle.

questions.question: Which part of the clavicle is most commonly fractured?

explanations.a: Fractures of the medial third are relatively uncommon.
explanations.b: The lateral third can be fractured, but it is less commonly affected than the middle third.
explanations.c: The middle third, particularly near the junction of the medial two-thirds and lateral one-third, is the most common site of clavicular fracture.
explanations.d: The acromial end is not the most common site of clavicular fracture.

questions.question: The conoid tubercle is located on the:

explanations.a: The conoid tubercle is not located at the medial end.
explanations.b: The conoid tubercle is located on the inferior surface of the lateral third of the clavicle.
explanations.c: The conoid tubercle is not located on the anterior border.
explanations.d: The conoid tubercle is located on the inferior, not superior, surface.

questions.question: Which structure is attached to the conoid tubercle of the clavicle?

explanations.a: The deltoid attaches to the lateral third of the clavicle but not specifically to the conoid tubercle.
explanations.b: The trapezius attaches to the posterior border of the lateral third of the clavicle.
explanations.c: The subclavius attaches to the subclavian groove on the inferior surface of the clavicle.
explanations.d: The conoid ligament attaches to the conoid tubercle and forms part of the coracoclavicular ligament.

explanations.a: Although the clavicle contributes to the protection of structures in the root of the neck, this is not its primary function.
explanations.b: The clavicle acts as a strut that supports and stabilizes the shoulder and keeps the upper limb away from the trunk.
explanations.c: The shoulder joint is formed mainly by the head of the humerus and the glenoid cavity of the scapula.
explanations.d: The clavicle does not primarily function in blood cell production.

questions.question: Which ossification feature is characteristic of the clavicle?

answers.c: First bone to start ossifying in the embryo
answers.d: Last bone to ossify in the body

explanations.a: The clavicle does not ossify exclusively by the endochondral method.
explanations.b: Although much of the clavicle develops by intramembranous ossification, it is not correct to state that it ossifies only by this method.
explanations.c: The clavicle is the first bone in the body to begin ossification, starting early during embryonic development.
explanations.d: The clavicle is not the last bone to begin ossification.
